endDate.description: Date on which the tournament ends

startDate.description: Date on which the tournament starts

tournamentSeriesId.description: The same tournament across its editions: the same value every year it is held, where tournamentId is one edition.

factory.description: The factory versions that created and last wrote this record. Formerly the `factory` extension.

createdVersion.description: Factory version that created the record; absent on records created before it was stamped

version.description: Factory version that last wrote the record

timeStamp.description: Engine clock (milliseconds since the epoch) at the last write

Tournament.$comment: OPEN, and this is a KNOWN GAP rather than a decision — closing it is blocked, not declined. Measured 2026-08-28 against the 16 TODS fixtures: 13 records carry `venueIds`, 6 carry `deleted`, and `dualMatchMetadata`, `associatedOrganisations`, `rootOrganisationId`, `tournamentExternalId` and a nested `tournamentRecord` each appear. Closing this definition today fails 14 of 16 fixtures. Each undeclared field must first be resolved as either a real CODES concept (declare it in `types/tournamentTypes.ts` AND here) or as legacy data (correct the fixtures), after which this should become `false` to match the other 51.

EntryRestriction.$comment: A condition on WHO may enter, beyond age/gender/rating. Advisory in v1: CODES holds no section roster or membership register, so `evaluable` defaults to undecidable and getParticipantEligibility reports indeterminate rather than guessing.

Extension.$comment: OPEN, deliberately and permanently. Extensions are CODES' escape hatch: `value` is unconstrained by design, and callers attach their own keys. This is the one exception that is not a backlog item.

endDate.description: Date on which the event ends

startDate.description: Date on which the event starts

DisciplineEnum.description: Sport/discipline. Open, sport-agnostic vocabulary — any well-formed value is accepted so new sports need no schema release (see disciplineConstants / planning/DISCIPLINE_EXTENSIBILITY.md). Constrain via the allowedDisciplines policy where a fixed list is required. Known values are listed in examples.

endDate.description: Date on which the draw ends

startDate.description: Date on which the draw begins

endDate.description: Date on which the matchUp ends

MatchUpSchedule.description: CODES first-class schedule attributes on a matchUp, the canonical written shape since 5.0.0. Each field here was historically a timeItem of the corresponding itemType (SCHEDULED_DATE, ASSIGN_COURT, ...). START_TIME / STOP_TIME / RESUME_TIME / END_TIME / END_DATE remain timeItems because matchUpDuration() walks the ordered history.
MatchUpSchedule.$comment: CLOSED, and lists only what the engine WRITES into the record. The TypeScript MatchUpSchedule carries an index signature for hydration-time outputs (startTime, endTime, endDate, courtName, venueName, isoDateString, milliseconds, scheduleConflict, the recovery-time fields); those are never written into a stored record, so they are deliberately absent here. A field added to setFirstClassOrTimeItem's attribute set, or written directly onto matchUp.schedule, must be added here or schemaValidation.test.ts fails on a scheduled record.

calledAt.description: ISO timestamp captured when the matchUp is deliberately called to court. Distinct from scheduledTime (plan) and the START_TIME timeItem (actual start).

scoredTime.description: ISO timestamp auto-captured the first time a matchUp receives a meaningful score or winningSide; cleared when the score is removed.

ScheduleLock.description: A director's declaration that a matchUp's placement is deliberate and must not be moved by bulk or automated scheduling. Presence of the object is the lock; `attributes` narrows it to specific placement fields (absent means the whole placement).

matchUpTypeOptions.description: Permitted encounter choices; no concrete matchUpType means the choice is unresolved.

Organisation.$comment: OPEN, and this is a KNOWN GAP rather than a decision — closing it is blocked, not declined. Measured 2026-08-28 against the 16 TODS fixtures: records carry `createdAt`, `updatedAt` and a nested `parentOrganisation`. Closing this definition today fails 14 of 16 fixtures. Each undeclared field must first be resolved as either a real CODES concept (declare it in `types/tournamentTypes.ts` AND here) or as legacy data (correct the fixtures), after which this should become `false` to match the other 51.

SanctionConstraints.description: Limits a sanctioning provider's rules set for one tournament: provider-defined, enforced by the factory, never derived by it.

SanctionEventConstraints.description: The limits for the events an entry matches: eventType always; eventName and categoryName when stated.

TournamentScheduling.description: The tournament's scheduling state. profile, dailyLimits and timing were the schedulingProfile, scheduleLimits and scheduleTiming extensions (read either way).

profile.description: The scheduling profile: which rounds are scheduled on which date at which venue, in order.

ScheduleProfileRound.description: A round (or one segment of it) in a scheduling profile. eventName, roundName and sortOrder are display attributes.

notBeforeTime.description: 'HH:MM': the earliest time the round may start.

TournamentScheduleTiming.description: The tournament's own matchUp format timing, consulted before its scheduling policy.

VenueTransitEntry.description: Minutes to get between two venues; symmetric unless oneWay.

TournamentSanction.$comment: What a governing body DECIDED about a competition — the instance model from #4710. Three orthogonal axes: decision (did the application succeed), recognition (what the body asserts), classification (what grade is conferred). Before this definition existed the property was declared {"type": "object"}, so a record carrying decision: 'BANANA' validated.

MonetaryAmount.$comment: All three fields are required together: an amount with no stated scale is readable at two scales 100x apart. NOTE this definition is $ref'd where a whole VALUE is a monetary amount (SanctionFee.fee, SanctionFee.maximum). It is deliberately NOT composed into PrizeMoney, PrizeMoneyAward or RegistrationEntryFee via allOf, even though those extend it in TypeScript: `allOf` + `additionalProperties: false` REJECTS the inherited fields, because additionalProperties only sees the properties declared alongside it. Those three inline the triple instead. Verified against ajv before choosing.

Venue.$comment: OPEN, and this is a KNOWN GAP rather than a decision — closing it is blocked, not declined. Measured 2026-08-28 against the 16 TODS fixtures: 7 records carry `parentOrganisation`, which `Venue` does not declare. Closing this definition today fails 14 of 16 fixtures. Each undeclared field must first be resolved as either a real CODES concept (declare it in `types/tournamentTypes.ts` AND here) or as legacy data (correct the fixtures), after which this should become `false` to match the other 51.

Disabled.description: Closed outright (true), or closed on the dates it names ({ dates }): disableCourts writes either on a court, disableVenues writes true on a venue

venueId.description: The venue this court belongs to. Written by addCourt on every court; declared here so a real record validates.

FlightProfile.$comment: Stored as event.flightProfile (CODES first-class; the flightProfile extension on older records). A draw's flight is the entry in flights whose drawId matches it; the draw carries only its flightNumber.

links.$comment: LEGACY: flight-based voluntary consolation (removed 2022-04-13); nothing writes it now.

SideExitProvenanceEntry.description: Why one side of a matchUp holds an exit it did not play: the status it was given, the upstream status that produced it, the matchUp that produced it, and every matchUp whose double exit claims a BYE on that side's drawPosition.

byeClaims.description: Retired (Mentat P58, 2026-10-22): no longer written or read; accepted so that stored records still validate.

PresenceAttestation.description: One recorded presence fact: an individual participant, present or gone, at a time, attested by someone.

RatingsExpectationRule.description: A side's expected result against its opponent: LOGISTIC, 1 / (1 + base^((O - R) / spread)) (base 10, spread 400 in most published methods; FIFA's men's ranking 600); LINEAR, 0.5 + the gap × slope with the gap clamped to ±cap (World Rugby: 0.05, 10); ORDERED_PROBIT, the expected value of the set result, Σ P(i) × resultValues(i), P from the standard normal at the cut-points shifted by scale × the gap (FIVB: 0.008).

RatingsKRule.description: K: one value for both sides (zero-sum), or FiveThirtyEight's numerator / (m + offset)^shape by the player's career matches m, which the caller passes as matchesPlayed.

RatingsActualRule.description: A side's actual result: WIN_LOSS (1 / 0.5 / 0), SETS_PLAYED_SHARE (Huang 2014: best of 3 1 or 2/3, best of 5 1, 0.8 or 0.6) or SCORE_SHARE (the share of the points, else games, else sets won).

RatingsMarginRule.description: A K multiplier by the margin of victory: World Football Elo's goal-difference steps, FiveThirtyEight's autocorrelation-corrected log margin (NHL, NFL) or power margin (NBA), Weighted Elo's winner game share, or World Rugby's threshold (× 1.5 above 15 points).

RatingsShootoutRule.description: A win in a shootout: a full win (FiveThirtyEight NHL, by one goal), or partial actual results (FIFA's men's ranking: 0.75 and 0.5).

RatingsPolicy.description: A ratings policy (POLICY_TYPE_RATINGS): how a dynamic rating moves on a result. Each rule encodes a published rating method, which source names.

source.description: The published method the policy encodes.

kByTier.description: K by the event's tier, then the tournament's, keyed system:value.

winnerMinimumGain.description: FIVB: a winner who would lose points gains this instead, and the loser loses it (0.01).

PolicyDefinitions.$comment: Policies keyed by policy type, the shape of the appliedPolicies extension value on a Tournament, Event, DrawDefinition or Structure (resolved tournament, then event, then draw, then structure; a later level replaces a policy type whole). Its keys are the policy types the factory defines (policyConstants). A policy type described only as an object is not yet modelled here; the modelled ones are closed. Not yet referenced by any record definition: policies are stored in the extension, whose value is unconstrained. See Mentat/planning/CODES_POLICY_DEFINITIONS.md for the path to a first-class attribute.

rankingPoints.$comment: Described by rankingPolicy.schema.json, a separate schema document; not repeated here.

SchedulingPolicy.description: A scheduling policy: matchUp timing, recovery, daily limits and the default scheduling period.

defaultPeriodLength.description: Minutes per scheduling period (Garman's L) for a run that does not state one. A run's own periodLength wins, then a profile round's own periodLength, then this.

SchedulingMinutes.description: Minutes by matchUp type: the matchUp's own type, else TEAM for a line of a TEAM event, else default. SINGLES_DOUBLES and DOUBLES_SINGLES are recovery minutes when the next matchUp changes type.

SchedulingRecoveryBand.description: A recovery band keyed on measured played minutes; the band without upTo is the catch-all.

SeedingPolicy.description: A seeding policy: seeds count by draw size, seed positioning and additional seeds.

seedingProfile.description: The object form, or the legacy bare positioning string the readers still honour.

drawTypes.description: Per-drawType overrides, keyed by drawType; consulted before the outer profile.

CompetitionPolicy.description: A competition policy: rating, pairing and victory rules for a dynamically paired competition.

ratingsPolicy.description: A ratings preset by name, or a ratings policy inline with a CONSTANT K: the form rating's expectation, K and actual result. Without one, kFactor and logisticScale, else POLICY_RATINGS_COMPETITION_FORM's 24 and 400.

RoundNamingPolicy.description: A round naming policy: how rounds are named and abbreviated.

roundNamingMap.description: Round name by the number of matchUps in the round (1: Final).

abbreviatedRoundNamingMap.description: Abbreviated round name by the number of matchUps in the round.

qualifyingFinishMap.description: A qualifying structure's final round names, by the number of matchUps.

stageConstants.description: Prefix for each stage (MAIN, QUALIFYING, CONSOLATION, PLAY_OFF).

ActionsStructurePolicy.description: The structures an actions policy entry matches (an empty or absent list matches all) and the actions it allows.

MatchUpActionsPolicy.description: A matchUp actions policy: which actions are offered, and participant and substitution rules.

key.description: An accessor path into the participant, e.g. person.nationalityCode.

directive.description: An id collection to separate on (pairParticipants, teamParticipants, ...).

AvoidancePolicy.description: An avoidance policy: which participant attributes are separated in positioning, and by how much.

RoundRobinTallyPolicy.$comment: OPEN, and this is a decision: the TypeScript RoundRobinTallyPolicy is deliberately extensible ([key: string]: unknown), and the tally readers take more members than the stored policies show. The members listed are those the readers take; closing it would reject a policy the engine accepts.
RoundRobinTallyPolicy.description: A round robin tally (standings) policy. validateTallyPolicy checks its values where it is saved.

$comment: CONVENTION: every object definition states `additionalProperties` EXPLICITLY, and the default is `false`. Every definition but the open ones listed in that test is closed. A closed definition is what makes a CODES field added to the TypeScript types but never mirrored here a LOUD failure rather than a silent one — the drift fixed in #4718 went unnoticed for exactly this reason on the open definitions. The open definitions each carry a `$comment` saying why. `codesSchemaConvention.test.ts` enforces both halves: no definition may omit the keyword, and the open set may not grow without updating that test.
